store.summary: Learn Morse the Koch way, play Morse games, key with a paddle on GPIO, send to your radio, decode CW
store.description: From Ask Elmer, askelmer.com. Learn letters: the Koch method, starting with K and M; each new character is played to you first, and the next unlocks when your last 60 answers are 90% right, with cheers from Elmer, Penny and Gus. Copy the code: messages built only from the characters you know, a little faster each round. Send the code: key words with the space bar, J/K paddles or a real paddle, and get your speed and a fist score. Park hunt: pick the band that's open for the time and distance, copy a park activator's call and exchange through static, fading and other stations. Key and send: an iambic A/B or straight-key keyer for a paddle wired to the GPIO pins (3.5 mm jack: dit GPIO22, dah GPIO26, ground), with sidetone and what you send decoded on screen. Send typed text or your paddle to a radio through an optocoupler on GPIO23, or to a QRP Labs QMX over one USB cable (CAT text and DTR keying). Transmit stays off until you switch it on, and lets go of a key held over 10 seconds. CW decoder: radio audio into the side jack, a USB sound card or a QMX's USB audio; the tone and speed are found automatically. Fn+H shows help.
